# DialogWright

> An open-source TypeScript framework for voice and chat agents that understand people and act safely. Callers talk naturally and the system maps what they mean to the right action: a fast decision model reads what was said and answers typed questions (judgments, never generated text). What the agent says and does is predictable: fixed lines, deterministic code that decides what happens next, and a policy gate on every action (identity level, scope, confirmation, attempt limits) whose decisions are written to a hash-chained audit log. Replies are fast. An app is a folder: YAML for what is data (intents, forms, prompts, policy, identity, slots, locales) and TypeScript for what runs (tools, form hooks, custom rules, and any slot no library type fits), joined by `defineApp`.

Pre-release; APIs will change, and nothing is published to npm yet. In this repository the packages are read from their TypeScript source; `pnpm -r build` writes the JavaScript a project installs, and `pnpm adopt:test` proves a project of its own works on the packed packages. Requires Node 22.19 or later and pnpm. An app imports only from `'dialogwright'`. Read CLAUDE.md before changing anything: the gate decides, a line is generated only where the app asks for it and never a prescribed one, the engine imports no app, no real personal data (555 phone numbers, invented names), and the engine package uses neutral vocabulary.

## Start here

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the three roles, the layout, the commands and the rules.
- [Your first app](docs/first-app.md): a guided first app from a paragraph (a small home services company's line, invented): the exact prompt to give an assistant with the create-app skill, what the skill asks (the business name, when the paragraph gives none) and produces (the worksheet, the app folder, the corpus, the scripted calls, the policy card, the adversarial suite), how to run it with no keys, record it with the owner's key and call it, and how to change the paragraph.
- [The create-app skill](.claude/skills/create-app/SKILL.md): building an app from a one-paragraph description, step by step, with a worksheet whose decisions lead to each option, an options index, verified patterns (identity, caller ID, a one-time code, delegates, confirmed writes, read-backs, checks that rule callers out, offers and consent to text, range rules, retries, transfers, routes and hours) and the corpus format. It starts from the scaffold, `pnpm create-app <name>` (add `--identity` for an app that verifies callers), which writes an app under `apps/<name>` that passes `pnpm check`, its tests and its regression as created, with a `CLAUDE.md` of its own.
- [docs/README.md](docs/README.md): the docs index: everything in this repository, where its documentation is, and every command.
- [The authoring guide](docs/guide/README.md), in chapters, one file per section; read one at a time, never the whole guide: [1. The folder](docs/guide/01-the-folder.md), [2. The files, one by one](docs/guide/02-the-files-one-by-one.md) (app.yaml with the number calling, business hours, the handoff's data and transfers; intents.yaml; forms.yaml with checks and sub-forms; prompts.yaml; policy.yaml; identity.yaml; routes.yaml; slots.yaml; fixtures/; kb/), [3. Policy and identity](docs/guide/03-policy-and-identity.md) (the rules, the identity ladder, redaction, what is recorded, testing the policy, the policy card, CODEOWNERS), [4. What stays in TypeScript](docs/guide/04-what-stays-in-typescript-and-why.md) (tools, a tool's reply checked), [5. Writing a slot](docs/guide/05-writing-a-slot.md) (library types first, code second; listening, offers, retries), [6. The form hooks](docs/guide/06-the-form-hooks.md) (and the start hook, predicates, `failSoft`), [7. `pnpm check`](docs/guide/07-checking-an-app-pnpm-check.md), [8. Locales](docs/guide/08-locales.md), [9. Configuration hashes](docs/guide/09-configuration-hashes.md), [10. Editor support](docs/guide/10-editor-support.md), [11. Walkthroughs](docs/guide/11-walkthroughs.md), [12. The knowledge base](docs/guide/12-the-knowledge-base.md), [13. Channels](docs/guide/13-channels.md), [14. Running it](docs/guide/14-running-it.md), [15. The adversarial suite](docs/guide/15-the-adversarial-suite.md). The guide was one page, `docs/authoring-an-app.md`, which now only points to the chapters.
- In a project of its own, outside this repository: `npm create dialogwright@latest <name>` (once published; until then, a project of its own on the packed package: `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm pack --pack-destination <folder>` in `packages/dialogwright`, then `pnpm create-app <name> --standalone --dir <a folder outside this repository> --dialogwright file:<the packed .tgz>` (`pnpm adopt:test --keep` makes two such projects and leaves them)) writes the scaffold's app as a project on the `dialogwright` package. There, read the project's own `CLAUDE.md` first; the docs are the installed package's, under `node_modules/dialogwright/docs/` (the guide's contents at `node_modules/dialogwright/docs/guide/README.md` and its chapters beside it, the slot types at `node_modules/dialogwright/docs/slots/README.md`, the first-app walkthrough at `node_modules/dialogwright/docs/first-app.md`), and the create-app skill is copied into the project at `.claude/skills/create-app/SKILL.md`, its links pointing at those pages. Never edit anything under `node_modules`. Its commands are `npx dialogwright <command>` (`check`, `regress`, `policy:matrix`, `configure`, `start`, `diagnose`, ...; `npx dialogwright help` lists them) where this repository says `pnpm <command>`, and an app's own script is `npm run <script>`. See [where to start](docs/guide/11-walkthroughs.md#where-to-start).
- [The knowledge base](docs/guide/12-the-knowledge-base.md): answers to general questions from short approved passages, chosen by meaning and spoken word for word (never generated): the `kb/` folder (kb.yaml, topics, passages, sources, locales, drafts, the log of approvals, the retrieval index), how a call uses it (nominate, select, resolve, speak; the retrieval budget), the `topic` slot, answers through the gate (a form's `answers:`, `kbAnswerTool`, facts read by code, account lines), informational passages, approval and staleness, building one from documents, retrieval settings, testing and what is recorded.
- [kb-author](packages/kb-author/README.md): the authoring tool, `@dialogwright/kb-author`: ingest a folder or a website into sources, draft passages with a model (the author's own key, never in CI), review them on a local page where a person approves, refresh the sources, rank the gaps.
- [Channels](docs/guide/13-channels.md): every option for serving an app, with its default and when to change it: carriers (`VOICE_PROVIDERS`: Twilio, Telnyx or both, each with its own secret, voice and recognizer), languages on the phone (`voice.numbers`, `voice.locales` with a voice and recognizer per carrier, a switch intent with `locale:`), the web chat (`CHAT`, `CHAT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `CHAT_IDLE_MS`, `CHAT_MAX_SESSIONS`; our own wire), sign-in (`CHAT_SIGNIN=none|jwt|mock`, `signIn.claim`, `principals.fromClaims`), the widget (`WIDGET`, `WIDGET_FILE`, its options and theme), the data a call or chat comes with (`callData`, 13.14), and where a handoff goes and what goes with it (`transfer`, ordered targets with SIP headers, 13.15).
- [Running it](docs/guide/14-running-it.md): on a machine you own, in the order a developer meets it: try it with no keys, `pnpm configure` (two keys: a carrier's and a model's), `pnpm start --tunnel quick` (a Cloudflare quick tunnel, no account), pointing the carrier, `pnpm diagnose`; then a machine that stays on (`ENV_FILE`, `pnpm service`, `/ready` and the drain, `SESSION_STORE=file:` so a restart resumes a call, `RESTART_PAUSE_S`, `SESSION_FSYNC`, `pnpm fallback`), the console from a phone (`CONSOLE_AUTH=token`, `pnpm console:link`, the access log), retention, updating, the full option table, and idempotent tools (`idempotent: true`, `ctx.idempotencyKey`). The website's guide, [running your own IVR on a machine you own](https://dialogwright.com/guides/home-server.html), is the same story step by step; [scaling out](https://dialogwright.com/guides/scaling.html) is what many servers add (Phase 8b, planned).
- [The adversarial suite](docs/guide/15-the-adversarial-suite.md): hostile calls generated from each app (announced injections, relationships claimed and not proven, off-scope requests, codes said aloud or never sent, hostile replies from every tool), each held to properties over its run, never to lines; app.yaml's `testing: { adversarial: on }` (a new app has it on) runs it with `regress`, and `regress --adversarial <id>` shows a case turn by turn.
- [The widget](packages/widget/README.md): `@dialogwright/widget`, the script a site embeds for web chat: options as `data-*` attributes or `DialogWright.mount`, CSS custom properties, every word, the client's events, reconnect and sign-in; `createChatClient` alone for a site's own interface.
- [Live checks](docs/live-checks.md): what only real carrier, model and identity accounts can confirm, as a checklist for the maintainer.
- [Design](docs/design.md): the idea, the roles, how policy and identity work, testing, channels (§10), the numbered roadmap.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): rules, pull requests, "Adding a slot type", "Adding a built-in policy rule", "Adding a retriever or an embedder", "Adding an extraction format", "Adding a voice provider" (implement `VoiceProvider`, fixtures from the carrier's docs, `runVoiceProviderConformance`, an end-to-end test, the registry) and "Adding a session store" (implement `server/stores/types.ts`, pass `runStoreContract`, register it for `SESSION_STORE`).
- [apps/clinic](apps/clinic/README.md): the example app to learn from (a fictional clinic's appointment line; no keys needed).
- [apps/utility](apps/utility/README.md): the second example app, a fictional electric utility's line built by an AI coding assistant from one paragraph: identity, a one-time code, delegates, confirmed writes, range rules, a policy card and a knowledge base (no keys needed; its recorded cassette replays offline).

## Slot types

A slot is one value a form collects. Most slots are configuration: name a type in the app's `slots.yaml` and give it options. The model never writes the value; code turns its answers into one. Each page lists every option with its type and default, the default question text, the outcomes, the prompts it needs, and starter examples.

- [Index of slot types](docs/slots/README.md): which type to use, and the types not built yet (`otp`, `time-slot`).
- [digits](docs/slots/digits.md): a number of a fixed shape (an account, a card, a tracking number).
- [choice](docs/slots/choice.md): one of a fixed list, with an advanced tier for names that sound alike.
- [date](docs/slots/date.md): a calendar day, ahead or back, with optional spans such as "next week".
- [birthdate](docs/slots/birthdate.md): a date of birth, heard whole or in part, masked by default.
- [name](docs/slots/name.md): the caller's own name.
- [record](docs/slots/record.md): one of the app's own records, chosen by what the caller says of it.
- [text](docs/slots/text.md): the caller's own words, kept as said.
- [topic](docs/slots/topic.md): which of the knowledge base's topics the caller asks about, chosen among those retrieval nominates.

## Policy and identity

`policy.yaml` is the whole of what the agent may do: one entry per action (a tool) with its identity `level` and its `rules`, run in order, the first failure deciding. `identity.yaml` (optional) says who the app serves and how a caller proves who they are. The rules are `identity`, `scope`, `role`, `confirmed`, `attempts`, `fields`, `dateInRange` (bounds such as `today`, `today+30`, a date, or a lookup reference), `limit`, `oneOf` and `noneOf` (a value one of, or none of, a list, as a form's checks ask), `callerNumber` (a number the call sends to is the caller's own, or one they confirmed), and `custom: <id>` for a rule of the app's own, written with `defineRule` and shipped with examples. Rules are recorded by name. See [section 3 of the authoring guide](docs/guide/03-policy-and-identity.md).

## Schemas

- `packages/dialogwright/schemas/*.schema.json`: the JSON Schema of every YAML file in an app folder (`app`, `intents`, `forms`, `prompts`, `policy`, `identity`, `routes`, `slots`, `locale-slots`, and for a `kb/` folder `kb-settings`, `kb-topics`, `kb-locale-topics`, `kb-passage`, `kb-source`, `kb-pending`). Generated from the zod schemas; never edit by hand. Every YAML file names its schema on its first line.

## Commands

- `pnpm install`
- `pnpm -r build`: each package's `dist/` (JavaScript and declarations), for a project that installs it; nothing in this repository needs it. `pnpm adopt:test`: the packages packed, a project of its own made from the packed `create-dialogwright` outside the repository, and its check, type check, tests and stub regression run.
- `pnpm check`: check every app folder under `apps/`: YAML against the schemas, cross-references to the code, prompts in every locale, the corpus. Prints one line per problem, `file:line:column  path  message  ->  fix`, and exits 1 on any. Act on the fix text.
- `pnpm create-app <name> [--identity] [--dir <path>] [--display <text>]`: a new app under `apps/<name>` from the template (`packages/dialogwright/templates/`), linked into the workspace; it passes `pnpm check`, its tests and its stub regression as created.
- `pnpm verify`: the type check and the tests together.
- `pnpm --filter dialogwright regress:testkit` and `pnpm --filter @dialogwright/example-clinic regress`: the regressions. Never regenerate a baseline or snapshot to make a test pass; a changed output is a finding to explain.
- `pnpm --filter dialogwright schemas`: regenerate the JSON Schemas after a schema change.
- `pnpm policy:matrix [dir...]`, `pnpm policy:card [dir...]`, `pnpm app:diagram [dir...]`: write `policy.matrix` (what the gate decides, for every action and kind of caller), `POLICY.md` (the policy in plain English with diagrams) and `APP-MAP.md` (intents, forms, slots, actions, rules and routes as diagrams). Deliberate: tests compare each with what the app generates, so a policy change is a diff to review; CI never writes them.
- `pnpm --filter dialogwright exec tsx src/define/cli.ts policy:convert <absolute folder>`: convert a policy.yaml or identity.yaml in the old table shape to the current one.
- `pnpm --filter dialogwright slot-docs`: regenerate the slot type pages after a type's options, README or examples change.
- `pnpm --filter dialogwright test slots/<type>`: run a slot type's tests, including the conformance kit.
- `pnpm kb:ingest <folder | file | url> --dir <app folder> [--depth N]`: documents or a website into `kb/sources/<doc>.yaml`, by section with provenance. `pnpm kb:draft [app folder]`: draft passages into `kb/pending` with a model (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, the author's own, from the environment or `.env`; refuses in CI; every draft must quote its source section word for word; nothing pending is ever said). `pnpm kb:review [app folder]`: the review page on 127.0.0.1 with a one-time token, where a person approves, edits or rejects. `pnpm kb:approve <id...> --by "<name>"` and `pnpm kb:status [dir]`: approve a passage or draft (only a person does), and list passages by state. `pnpm kb:refresh [app folder]`: read the sources again and withhold what changed. `pnpm kb:gaps [app folder] [--traces <path>]`: what callers asked that nothing answered, ranked. `pnpm kb:model`, `pnpm kb:index [dir]`, `pnpm kb:bakeoff <dir> --paraphrases <file> [--sweep]`: the embedding model, the committed index of topic vectors, and the retrieval bake-off with the floor and cap sweep.
- `pnpm --filter @dialogwright/example-clinic cli --client heuristic`: a text console for the clinic, with no keys.
- `pnpm --filter @dialogwright/example-utility serve` with `PUBLIC_HOST=localhost CHAT=on CHAT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000 CHAT_SIGNIN=mock WIDGET=on` (after `pnpm --filter @dialogwright/widget build`): the web chat and the widget on a laptop, at `http://localhost:3000/chat-demo`.
- `pnpm configure [--app <name>]`, `pnpm start [--app <name>] [--tunnel quick|named|none]`, `pnpm diagnose [--app <name>] [--offline]`: the first hour on a machine you own: settings written with two keys (or none, to try it; a key is never a flag), the server behind a quick tunnel, and what is misconfigured. A settings file kept elsewhere is named with `ENV_FILE=<path>` in front. `ENV_FILE=<path> pnpm service <launchd|systemd> --app <name>`: a service file that keeps it running. `pnpm fallback --provider <twilio|telnyx> --number <E.164> --out <file>`: what the carrier plays when the server is down. `pnpm console:link`: a one-time console sign-in link (with `CONSOLE_AUTH=token`). `pnpm audit:verify <audit folder>`: each audit day's hash chain.
- `pnpm --filter @dialogwright/widget build`: the widget's script, `packages/widget/dist/dialogwright-widget.js` (and `.mjs`), for a site to load from its own CDN.
- The real decision model (`--client jev`, `--client record`, `JEV_CLIENT=jev`) needs a key: TypeSafe (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, the default), OpenRouter or the Vercel AI Gateway (`JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter|vercel`), or a compatible endpoint (`JEV_PROVIDER=custom`, `JEV_BASE_URL`, `JEV_MODEL`, optional `JEV_API_KEY`; its probabilities are not Jev's, so measure thresholds with its own cassette). Each model records its own cassette. An app's `.env.example` lists the variables; never commit a key.
